sec: Thionamides, RAI and surgical management of thyrotoxicosis

items.q: Match the following thionamide feature — 1) Methimazole 2) Propylthiouracil 3) Carbimazole 4) Block-and-replace regimen … A) Preferred in most adults B) Preferred in T1 pregnancy and thyroid storm C) Prodrug of methimazole D) Thionamide + levothyroxine combination
items.exp: Methimazole is preferred in non-pregnant adults; PTU is reserved for T1 pregnancy and thyroid storm; carbimazole is the prodrug of methimazole; block-and-replace is a thionamide-plus-levothyroxine combination. (Book p912)

items.q: A woman in the first trimester of pregnancy needs treatment for Graves disease. Which thionamide is the most appropriate?
items.exp: PTU is preferred in T1 because methimazole is associated with embryopathy; methimazole is preferred from T2 onward. (Book p912)

items.q: Assess thionamide adverse effects: I Agranulocytosis is a rare but serious idiosyncratic reaction. II Methimazole carries a black-box warning for hepatotoxicity in T1 pregnancy.
items.exp: Agranulocytosis is a rare idiosyncratic reaction with both thionamides; PTU carries the hepatotoxicity warning (especially in T1 pregnancy), not methimazole. (Book p912)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a side-effect not typical of methimazole?
items.exp: Severe hepatotoxicity with hepatic failure is the PTU-type pattern; methimazole typically causes cholestatic liver enzyme rise, not severe hepatotoxicity. (Book p912)

items.q: The thionamide dose in Graves disease is adjusted aiming for ___.
opts: Free T4 / free T3 normalisation before TSH recovery
items.exp: Free T4/T3 normalise earlier than TSH; dose is titrated to free hormones with TSH as a delayed check. (Book p912)

items.q: Match the following definitive therapy — 1) Radioactive iodine ablation 2) Total thyroidectomy 3) Antithyroid drugs … A) Definitive in selected patients with low ophthalmopathy risk B) Rapid control in pregnancy and large goitres C) Long-term remission in ~50% of Graves patients
items.exp: RAI is definitive when eye disease is inactive; surgery is preferred in pregnancy with large goitres or rapid control; thionamides achieve long-term remission in about half of patients. (Book p912)

items.q: A patient with Graves disease has active moderate ophthalmopathy and a large goitre. Which definitive therapy is most appropriate?
items.exp: Active ophthalmopathy and large goitre favour thyroidectomy; RAI should be covered with steroids in active eye disease. (Book p912)

items.q: Assess RAI: I It is contraindicated in pregnancy and breastfeeding. II It can cause thyroiditis and transient thyrotoxicosis.
items.exp: RAI is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy and breastfeeding; post-RAI thyroiditis can cause transient thyrotoxicosis before hypothyroidism. (Book p912)

items.q: Match the following adjunct — 1) Beta-blocker 2) NSAID 3) Calcium supplementation 4) Cholestyramine … A) Symptomatic control of adrenergic symptoms B) Analgesia in subacute thyroiditis C) Bone protection in chronic thyrotoxicosis D) Reduces enterohepatic recycling of thyroid hormone
items.exp: Beta-blockers control adrenergic symptoms; NSAIDs are analgesics in subacute thyroiditis; calcium supports bone in chronic thyrotoxicosis; cholestyramine reduces enterohepatic recycling of thyroid hormone. (Book p912)

items.q: A patient on methimazole develops sore throat and fever; total neutrophil count is 0.4 × 10⁹/L. The next step is:
opts: Stop methimazole immediately and admit for neutropenic sepsis work-up
Continue methimazole and add G-CSF as outpatient
Add lithium to boost white cells (alternative)
items.exp: Agranulocytosis requires immediate cessation of the thionamide and urgent management of neutropenic sepsis risk. (Book p912)

items.q: The block-and-replace regimen pairs a thionamide with ___ to avoid hypothyroidism.
items.exp: Block-and-replace uses a fixed thionamide dose plus levothyroxine to maintain euthyroidism during the block. (Book p912)

items.q: Assess treatment duration: I Antithyroid drug course is typically 12–18 months. II Most Graves patients achieve permanent remission with thionamides alone.
items.exp: A typical course is 12–18 months; permanent remission occurs in roughly half of patients, not most. (Book p912)
